manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the bottle on the table and lift it.

Task description: The target is the white bottle with a light-colored cap on the left side of the table. Use the available right arm to grasp and lift it off the table.

Success criteria: The bottle is lifted with its base clear of the table and its body nearly vertical, cap up and base down.

## Execution tips

- Grasp a relatively straight section of the bottle body below the shoulder and above the base, giving both pads full contact. Avoid the cap and sloped shoulder to reduce slipping or an off-center grasp.
- Open slightly wider than the selected bottle section and leave fingertip clearance above the table. Confirm the fingers actually lie on opposite sides before closing rather than inferring alignment from image overlap and pushing the bottle over from one side.
- Preserve the bottle's upright orientation while lifting smoothly. If it slides downward or tilts significantly, restore table support under its bottom before adjusting rather than releasing in midair.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start a single real-robot episode with your given parameters and act on the returned manual and live observations. When finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode.

I have read the manual and confirmed the target is the upright white bottle with a light-colored cap on the left. I am opening the gripper and aligning with its middle, then will refine in small steps nearby and test-lift once secure.

The bottle remains upright and has not been touched. The wrist joint is near its rotation limit, so I will make a small adjustment to the gripper's downward angle before continuing to align in small steps.

The wrist adjustment is complete, and the gripper remains open. Next I will advance along the approach direction in centimeter steps, using both cameras to confirm the bottle body is between the pads before closing.

After a half-centimeter test lift, the bottle remains on the table, so a secure grasp has not been established. I will reopen the gripper, move it deeper around both sides of the bottle, then test again.
The bottle remains standing steadily in its original position. I increased the approach depth and am lowering the grasp point to a straighter section of the body, checking clearance gradually.

The gripper has contacted the bottle body, but the actual opening is now at the target value; I still need to confirm it is secure. I will make one more half-centimeter test lift and observe whether the bottle moves with the gripper.

After this closure, the actual gripper opening is about 46 mm, slightly above the 45 mm target, indicating resistance. I will now lift slightly to check whether the bottle bottom clears the table and inspect its pose.

The test lift has not yet confirmed that the bottle cleared the table. I am maintaining its horizontal position and lowering the gripper further so the pads avoid the shoulder; the bottle remains upright without visible tipping.

The bottle has moved upward continuously with the gripper, whose actual opening is stable at about 60 mm; the bottle bottom is visibly off the table. Its cap is up and bottom down. I will gently raise it a little more, briefly observe stability, then end the episode.
